items.title: Harold Dejan Interview, 1960-10-14
items.q: I was playing with him with the Liberty Band

ctx.x: Well, you mentioned outside some, who was it that Saeed's brother-in-law or something? Oh, Benny Benoit.

I was playing with him with the Liberty Band, but I gnawly passed. That's years ago. I remember when I gnawly passed and myself, we were playing at the Crystal Palace in Depression time up on Clio and Radha, near Drys. And all the boys from Browns, the ice cream company used to come there, you know. And I know I told him, son, you don't drink now. I said, no, son. He said, well, don't turn no beer on. When they bring you the beer, give it to me. When the boys bring the ice cream, I give it to you. So, I ate the…
And it sounds like, who did you say?

items.title: Harold Dejan Interview, 1960-11-18
items.q: He was playing with me at the Five Island again

ctx.x: See because if he lived with his sister she could remember a lot of stuff. He was a very good banjo player. He was playing with me at the Five Island again, see you see. Very good banjo player.
We have about another minute or so on here. Yeah, well. Is there anything else you can tell about when you were young to finish up your life?

items.title: Harry Fairconnetue Interview, 1962-11-11
items.q: He and I, two altos, Benny Benoit and Banjo.

ctx.x: Oh yeah, he stayed with them for a while.
I mean Cuckoo and Big Ike, you know. He and I, two altos, Benny Benoit and Banjo. Oh yeah.
Tell me about that time, Harold, I gotta get this done, about that drink of whiskey. We were talking about on the way over here, about this man wanting you to drink with him.
